record.paper_title: Nicholson's blowflies differential equations revisited: Main results and open problems
record.original_question: For the distributed-delay Nicholson model dN/dt = -d N(t) + P integral from h(t) to t of N(u) exp(-N(u)) d_u R(t,u), determine sufficient conditions on the model parameters and delay distribution such that the inequality P < d e guarantees the existence of at least one rapidly oscillating solution about the positive equilibrium N* = ln(P/d). Here rapid oscillation should be understood in the sense used for Nicholson-type delay equations: eventually the distance between adjacent zeros of N(t)-N* does not exceed the relevant delay.

evidence.quote: The solution is rapidly oscillating if eventually the distance between adjacent zeros of the function does not exceed the delay.
Find sufficient conditions on the parameters of Eq. (21) such that the condition P < de implies existence of a rapidly oscillating solution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the scalar distributed-delay Nicholson blowflies equation
  dN(t)/dt = -d N(t) + P ∫_{h(t)}^{t} N(u) e^{-N(u)} d_u R(t,u),  t ≥ t_0,
where d > 0 and P > 0 are constants, h: [t_0, ∞) → ℝ is a continuous nondecreasing delay function with h(t) ≤ t and lim_{t→∞} h(t) = ∞, and for each t the map u ↦ R(t,u) is nondecreasing on [h(t), t] with R(t,t) - R(t,h(t)) = 1, so that the integral is a probability-weighted average of N(u) e^{-N(u)} over the delay window [h(t), t]. Assume P > d so that the equation admits the positive equilibrium N* = ln(P/d).

A solution N(t) is called rapidly oscillating about N* if there exists T such that for all t ≥ T, any two consecutive zeros t_1 < t_2 of N(t) - N* satisfy t_2 - t_1 ≤ t_2 - h(t_2) (i.e. the distance between adjacent zeros is at most the prevailing delay).

Problem: Find sufficient conditions on the parameters d, P and on the delay distribution (h, R) such that the inequality
  P < d·e
implies the existence of at least one rapidly oscillating solution of the equation about N*.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in surveys revisiting Nicholson's blowflies equations. While rapidly oscillating solutions have been studied for the constant-delay Nicholson equation, no published resolution of the distributed-delay version under the threshold P < de was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: Nicholson's blowflies differential equations revisited: Main results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey covering permanence, oscillation, local and global stability of solutions for Nicholson's blowflies equation, listing open problems for the distributed-delay model.
status_evidence.claim: The rapidly-oscillating-solution question for the distributed-delay Nicholson equation is listed among open problems.

status_evidence.title: Nicholson's blowflies equation with a distributed delay
status_evidence.snippet: Study of the distributed-delay Nicholson equation; addresses stability and oscillation but does not resolve sufficient conditions for rapidly oscillating solutions under P<de.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the rapidly oscillating solution problem under P<de is provided.
